hypotheses.justification: `Module.rankAtStalk M p` is defined as `finrank (Localization.AtPrime p.asIdeal) (LocalizedModule p.asIdeal.primeCompl M)`. The proof only uses flatness (and finite presentation) to get local constancy of the rank, which lets it reduce to p = ⊥. That reduction is not needed. Since S is a domain, every x ∈ p.asIdeal.primeCompl is nonzero, because 0 ∈ p. So `p.asIdeal.primeCompl ≤ nonZeroDivisors S` holds for every prime p. The `hle` argument in the proof then works for any p. `IsLocalization.rank_eq` and `IsLocalizedModule.rank_eq` (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Dimension/Localization.lean) need only `hp : p ≤ R⁰`. They give `rank (S_p) (M_p) = rank S M = n`, and `finrank_eq_of_rank_eq` finishes. The theorem is therefore true and provable without Flat.

The same direct argument works for every prime p. `primeCompl p ≤ nonZeroDivisors S` holds in a domain. `IsLocalization.rank_eq` and `IsLocalizedModule.rank_eq` need no finite presentation, only `hp : p ≤ R⁰`. So `rank (S_p) (M_p) = rank S M = n`, and `finrank_eq_of_rank_eq` gives the result. Finite presentation was used in the original proof only for `isLocallyConstant_rankAtStalk`, which is no longer needed. Both this and Flat can be deleted, individually or together.
